articles.summary: RANGIA: A woman was found dead with injury marks on her throat in a hotel near Rangia railway station in Assam’s Kamrup district on Sunday, a police o.
articles.body: RANGIA: A woman was found dead with injury marks on her throat in a hotel near Rangia railway station in Assam’s Kamrup district on Sunday, a police officer said.A man who had booked the hotel room and was found inside with the woman’s body was arrested on murder charges, a police officer told news agency PTI.The victim was identified from her Aadhaar card as Malini Guria, a resident of Asurmarigaon village in Sonitpur district, the officer said.According to hotel owner Dhrubajyoti Saloi, the accused, Avijit Kindo, had booked two rooms at the hotel on Saturday evening, saying three of his friends would stay in one room while he would stay in the other.On Sunday morning, two women staying in one of the rooms were preparing to leave when they told the hotel staff that their friend in the other room was not responding to their calls, although a man was answering, police said.The hotel owner knocked on the door, but the occupant refused to open it. He then immediately alerted the police.A police team reached the hotel and compelled the occupant to open the door, where they found the woman’s blood-stained body lying on the bed with injury marks on her throat, the officer said.A piece of cloth was found hanging from the ceiling fan, while the man was sitting on the bed with scissors and a screwdriver, he added.According to officer-in-charge of Rangia Police Station Mintu Baro, the accused, who has been taken into custody, confessed to the crime before police.Preliminary inquiry suggests that the crime may be linked to a love affair, police said.The officer said the women had come from Chennai, where they work for a private company.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news. articles.title: Launch of Atari’s 'ET, the Extra-Terrestrial' is considered as biggest flop in video game history, leading to Atari’s 'death', but it left an 'El Paso warehouse mystery' that continues to haunt
articles.summary: Tech News News: ​Atari released E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial in 1982, and it is considered one of the worst failures in video game history. By then, Atari was experienc.
articles.body: ​Atari released E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial in 1982, and it is considered one of the worst failures in video game history. By then, Atari was experiencing financial difficulties, with falling console sales and increased competition. Unsold copies of the game were discovered in a warehouse in El Paso and were rumoured to have been disposed of in a landfill in Alamogordo, New Mexico. The landfill's location remained a mystery for many years.​The mystery unfolded in 2014, when a dig at a New Mexico landfill led to the discovery of 1,382 Atari game cartridges, including games such as "E.T.", "Centipede", and "Pac-Man". The discovery confirmed the myth that some of the company's games were dumped at the landfill; it also raised questions about the landfill's size, since the digging was not extensive enough. From a failure of business, it became a mystery of the "El Paso warehouse".​How Atari’s “E.T.” game became a huge problem​“E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial” was launched by Atari before Christmas in 1982, at a time when Atari was having a hard time in the market. Competing games were taking over the market, the console was no longer popular, and reviews were poor.​Sales fell far below Atari’s initial projections, leaving large numbers of copies sitting unsold in the company’s El Paso warehouse. With little prospect of selling the remaining inventory, Atari eventually sent the cartridges to New Mexico for disposal.​This was one aspect of the mystery of this dumping. Reports immediately following the incident said Atari dumped the games, and even Atari officials at the time referred to the dumping. However, the specific location and number of games were not known.​The Atari cartridge dump mystery​James Heller, an Atari employee involved in disposing of the games, later provided a detailed account of what happened. In a Q&A with an Atari ephemera-based blog, Heller said that in 1983 he brought 12 truckloads containing 728,000 cartridges to a site measuring about 50 by 100 feet.​After three days of dumping, Heller stated that they had laid six truckloads of concrete over the spot, as children were found scavenging for cartridge cases there. But even this much concrete was not sufficient to cover up all the games.​“I would say that 95 percent of the cartridges dumped were new,” Heller said. “There were a number of different titles.”​His report gave archaeologists a definitive spot to dig, but it would take years to figure out whether the legendary Atari cartridge dump really had the millions of cartridges eyewitnesses claimed.​Archaeologists finally dug into the landfill​The project, in which Andrew Reinhard was one of the archaeologists, was filmed in 2014 in collaboration with Fuel Entertainment, Lightbox, and Microsoft. The filming crew was given permission to dig at the Alamogordo landfill; however, they were allowed to do so for only two days on four acres of the total 300-acre site.​Although the digging area was small, they dug up to 30 feet into the trash pile and retrieved 1,382 Atari game cartridges, along with other pieces of equipment.​The first discovery was a boxed copy of “E.T.” that still contained its game instructions, catalogue and a “Raiders of the Lost Ark” insert. Reinhard later described finding more games and hardware as the excavation continued, with thousands of cartridges representing dozens of titles being exposed.​A sandstorm eventually halted the excavation. The trench containing the games was photographed, while thousands of recovered objects were collected for analysis and cataloguing.​What was found beneath the New Mexico dump​The excavation confirmed that “E.T.” cartridges had been buried at the site, but the discovery wasn't limited to Atari's infamous game. Archaeologists also found copies of “Centipede,” “Pac-Man” and other titles, along with additional Atari equipment.​In 1983, Joe Lewandowski, who worked for the company responsible for collecting waste from the site, observed the dumping of the material. With Heller's help, he guided the filmmakers and the excavation team to the spot where the cartridges were buried.​Only 1.3% of the landfill had been investigated; thus, the 1,382 cartridges found were only a fraction of what could have been found in the whole landfill.​The Atari cartridges became collectors’ items​Some of the recovered cartridges eventually found their way into collections and auctions. Lewandowski said he auctioned several pieces and raised more than $100,000 for local institutions, including a library and a museum.​An “E.T.” cartridge was also given by Fuel Entertainment to the Smithsonian Institution. While the game is stored at the American History Museum, it is not currently on display.​Thus, this archaeological dig answered one side of the years-old controversy: Atari did indeed bury thousands of cartridges in the Alamogordo landfill, and “E.T.” cartridges were among them. However, because only a tiny fraction of the landfill was excavated, the extent of what lay underground was never determined.​For a game that became associated with Atari's collapse, the buried cartridges eventually became something else—a physical record of one of the video game industry's most famous failures, and the answer to a mystery that had survived for more than 30 years.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Chinese FM Wang Yi stepped in for Xi at PM Modi’s Brics gala dinner: Reports
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Amid reports that Chinese president Xi Jinping skipped the Brics gala dinner hosted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi, China was.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Amid reports that Chinese president Xi Jinping skipped the Brics gala dinner hosted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi, China was represented at the high-profile gathering by foreign minister Wang Yi on Saturday.The dinner was hosted by Modi at Bharat Mandapam, the venue of the 18th Brics Summit, and was attended by Brics leaders, senior delegates from participating countries and representatives of international organisations.Wang, who is part of the Chinese delegation attending the summit, represented China at the dinner, news agency ANI reported, quoting sources. The reason for Xi’s absence was not immediately known. However, earlier another source cited by news agency PTI had suggested that the Chinese president had returned to his hotel to rest.Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed, who had attended the summit earlier in the day, was also among the notable absentees after leaving for home.Russian president Vladimir Putin and other leaders of the Brics attended the dinner. Union ministers and the chief ministers of several states were also present on the occasion.Xi, who arrived in New Delhi on Saturday afternoon, had attended the Brics Leaders’ Summit proceedings earlier in the day and held a bilateral meeting with Modi on the sidelines.During the meeting, Xi said India and China should approach their relationship from a long-term strategic perspective.“China-India relations have developed, with both sides keeping in mind the long-term development of bilateral relations from a strategic perspective,” Xi said.He added that despite differences, the two countries had been able to “support and help each other to achieve common development.”Xi also noted that it was his second visit to New Delhi in 12 years and that the two leaders had met more than 20 times during that period, resulting in “a series of important consensuses”.Modi, meanwhile, thanked China for its support during India’s Brics chairship.“It gives me great pleasure to extend a warm welcome to you. Thank you very much for your positive remarks at the Brics Summit. I express my gratitude for the support and cooperation received from China during India's Brics chairmanship,” Modi said.“We now have the opportunity to discuss bilateral cooperation. Once again, a warm welcome to India,” he added.The two sides also reaffirmed their commitment to a “fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable resolution” of the India-China boundary question and said differences should not become disputes. The Ministry of External Affairs said both sides stressed the need for “mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest.” The Chinese president on Sunday left New Delhi after attending the Summit.Meanwhile, the gala dinner featured a menu showcasing regional Indian cuisine, including Khandvi Mille-Feuille, Khumb Galouti, Paneer Lababdar, Gucchi Marmik, millet pulao, beetroot raita, jalebi and Shahtoot Phirni.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Another Polish hiker dies in High Tatra mountain range
articles.summary: Another Polish mountaineer has died in an accident in the High Tatra mountains that straddle Poland and Slovakia. The climber, 35, fell from a steep rock fac...
articles.body:
Another Polish mountaineer has died in an accident in the High Tatra mountains that straddle Poland and Slovakia.

The climber, 35, fell from a steep rock face below Gerlach Peak, the Czech news agency CTK reported on Sunday, citing the Slovak mountain rescue service.

The deceased climber's 40-year-old companion witnessed the accident. He was unable to continue the descent unaided afterwards.

A rescue helicopter landed at the scene but could only confirm the man's death. The crew brought the body and the surviving hiker to Stary Smokovec, one of the main towns in the central part of the High Tatras in northern Slovakia.

At 2,655 metres, Gerlach Peak is the highest peak in the High Tatras.

At the beginning of August, two Polish climbers died in accidents on the Slovak side of the High Tatras. Also at that time, two other Polish climbers died while hiking on the Polish side of the mountain range.

articles.title: India builds Brics without breaking up with US
articles.summary: US News: TOI correspondent from Washington: It’s a club MAGA boss Donald Trump loves to hate -- one that New Delhi not only refuses to leave but wants to lead..
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: It’s a club MAGA boss Donald Trump loves to hate -- one that New Delhi not only refuses to leave but wants to lead. As India hugged Brics without breaking up with America, presiding over a geopolitical game of musical chairs where nobody gets eliminated, reviews in Washington of the just-concluded summit sounded more wary than alarmed despite the group's growing strength and a reprimand of Uncle Sam without calling him by name.While the New Delhi Declaration took aim at unilateral tariffs, trade barriers, and sanctions, warning that such measures distort global commerce and violate the spirit of the WTO -- while dancing around the issue of wars involving the US, Russia, and several members -- the reaction in Washington to the summit has been more hmmm than horror. The broad consensus in the American commentariat is that Brics is acquiring political heft, but remains far too divided to become a coherent anti-American alliance.Time went so far as to headline its assessment “Why a Divided Brics Poses No Challenge to America,” while emphasizing that India, the summit host, still wants Brics to accomplish things without antagonizing Washington. “Brics leaders gather in New Delhi as wars and rivalries strain the expanded bloc,” noted the Washington Post, while the NYT observed that while “China wants Brics to challenge American power, India wants it broad enough that countries don't have to choose.”Also read: Brics diplomacy: Iran president says Tehran, UAE want to 'turn the page' on warThat may well be the central paradox of the New Delhi summit: Brics is becoming bigger, louder, and more confident about challenging Western dominance, while one of its key, pivotal members is simultaneously deepening ties with Washington. The Modi-Xi encounter was therefore watched especially closely, even more than the Modi-Putin engagement with one wag -- referring to the Galwan flare-up -- characterizing it as a diplomatic equivalent of reopening a restaurant that had been closed after a rather serious kitchen fire.Several analysts noted that Beijing's longstanding concern has been India's growing alignment with the U.S. “China wants to shape India’s strategic choice. It wants an India that does not see China as a threat. It also wants India to not side with the US by default because of China,” Stimson Center’s Yun Sun told FT, whose headline, "World’s biggest relationship? Xi and Modi look to rebuild ties for 2.8bn people" emphasized the size of the two nations.Jeffrey Sachs, the Columbia University economist and prominent critic of U.S. foreign policy, made the argument much more emphatically. In an interview ahead of the summit, he said: “India and China together can really make a multilateral world,” describing their cooperation as central to the emergence of a genuinely multipolar order, while noting that Brics represents roughly half the world's population and economic output. Sachs, in fact, has gone further in pushing for an Asian partnership, arguing that “India should leave the Quad, period.”Also read: 'I don't care': Trump on Gulf-Iran talks at Brics SummitHowever, New Delhi, which seems quite happy to collect diplomatic memberships the way some people collect airline miles, is staying on as a member of a rather moribund Quad while using its Brics chairmanship to portray itself as a leading voice of the Global South. PM Modi is expected to attend the G20 leaders' summit to be hosted by President Trump in Miami December 14-15.Then there was Modi-Putin tango that has long irked traditionalist foreign policy boffins in the U.S. The Russian president's appearance alongside Modi provided another visual rebuttal to the US idea that Moscow has been diplomatically quarantined, with the optics of Putin, Xi, Modi and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in the same frame demonstrating that Russia's international relationships is more durable that U.S would like to believe. If anything, some analysts noted that Trumpian Washington was the one getting isolated – or isolating itself. “Trump gets wrecked at Brics,” read the headline for in MeidasTouch, a trenchantly anti-Trump vlog.Still, American analysts are hardly proclaiming the arrival of a Brics era or empire. While the expanded grouping now accounts for about half the world's population, roughly 40% of global GDP and more than a quarter of global trade, one analyst smirked that Brics also looks like a family reunion where several relatives have hired lawyers. India and China remain strategic competitors; Iran and the UAE have sharply different interests; and Saudi Arabia and Iran have their own complicated history.So Washington takes comfort in the fact that Brics has not displaced the dollar, created a common currency or produced anything resembling Nato in reverse – things that President Trump growled against. Which is probably why, with its eminence grise out causing ripples in Ireland, there was no substantive public White House or State Department statement about the summit.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Mamata's TMC faction names candidates for Nandigram, Rejinagar bypolls in Bengal
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Trinamool Congress (TMC) faction led by Mamata Banerjee on Sunday announced Sanchita Pradhan (Dey) and Rabiul Alam Chowdhury as its can.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Trinamool Congress (TMC) faction led by Mamata Banerjee on Sunday announced Sanchita Pradhan (Dey) and Rabiul Alam Chowdhury as its candidates for the October 6 bypolls to the Nandigram and Rejinagar assembly seats, respectively. The counting of votes is set to take place on October 9.Pradhan is a new face, while Chowdhury is a former MLA, news agency PTI reports.The announcement comes after an earlier rebel TMC faction said it would support Mamata Banerjee, strengthening the party's position ahead of the bypolls.The Nandigram bypoll was necessitated after Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari vacated the seat and chose to retain Bhabanipur, where he defeated TMC chief Mamata Banerjee in the Assembly elections held earlier this year. The Rejinagar seat fell vacant after Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) founder Humayun Kabir resigned from the seat, having also won from Nowda.The two seats are expected to witness a keen political contest, with the bypoll results likely to be closely watched ahead of the next electoral battle in the state.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
